item.title: Iran's buried Pickaxe Mountain site looms over nuclear talks
item.description: As the United States and Iran inch toward a possible deal ahead of the April 22 ceasefire deadline, a deeply buried nuclear facility near Natanz known as Pickaxe Mountain has emerged as one of the most contentious obstacles to any lasting agreement — and some analysts and Iran hawks are pressing President Trump to consider extreme measures to destroy it.

item.title: Iran threatens to reclose Strait of Hormuz if US blockade continues
item.description: Hours after declaring the Strait of Hormuz fully reopened to commercial shipping, Iran warned on Friday that it could shut the waterway again if the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

item.title: Israeli drone kills one in southern Lebanon hours into ceasefire
item.description:
An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in southern Lebanon on Friday, killing one person on the first full day of a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire, even as President Trump declared on social media that Israel was "PROHIBITED" from bombing Lebanon.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that a motorcyclist was killed in the town of Kounine, in the Bint Jbeil district, after being targeted by an Israeli drone. The Lebanese army reported additional violations on Friday morning, including intermittent shelling of several southern villages and firing on an ambulance team in Kounine.

item.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza
item.description: UNICEF said Friday it was "outraged" after two truck drivers it contracted to deliver clean water to families in the Gaza Strip were killed by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. Two others were injured in the incident, which occurred during routine water trucking operations early Friday morning, according to the agency's statement.

item.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver
item.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.

item.title: China reaches 125 GW to become world's largest nuclear power
item.description: China has claimed the top spot globally for total installed nuclear power capacity, reaching 125 gigawatts, according to a blue book released Friday by the China Nuclear Energy Association. The milestone underscores Beijing's accelerating push to expand its atomic energy fleet at a pace unmatched by any other nation.

item.title: Australia, Japan sign $7B stealth frigate deal
item.description: Australia and Japan on Saturday signed contracts launching a A$10 billion (US$7 billion) deal to supply Australia with advanced stealth frigates, in what has been described as Japan's most consequential defense export agreement since World War II.

item.title: Iran's 'mosquito fleet' holds Hormuz despite 155 warships sunk
item.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, U.S. and allied strikes have sunk more than 155 Iranian naval vessels and wiped out entire classes of warships. Yet the fleet Tehran relies on most to control the Strait of Hormuz — a sprawling armada of small, fast boats operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps — remains largely intact and continues to menace one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.

item.title: Iranians fear regime will tighten grip once ceasefire holds
item.description:
Iranians struggling to piece together daily life after weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes and a brutal crackdown on protesters are gripped by fear that conditions will only worsen once the guns fall silent, even as a fragile ceasefire offers a momentary reprieve.

"The war will end, but that's when our real problems with the system begin," a 37-year-old named Fariba who took part in the January unrest told Reuters by phone from Iran. "I'm very afraid that if the regime reaches an agreement with the United States, it will increase pressure on ordinary people."

item.title: Iranians face 50th day of internet blackout as ceasefire nears expiration
item.description: As a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran inches toward its April 22 expiration, Iranians are navigating a precarious existence shaped by weeks of aerial bombardment, a brutal government crackdown on mass protests, and an economic crisis with no clear end in sight. The pause in fighting has brought a measure of relief — but for many, it has also sharpened fears that the worst may still lie ahead.

item.title: Egypt, Pakistan building framework for lasting US-Iran peace
item.description:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed on Saturday that Egypt and Pakistan are working closely together on a framework to secure a lasting peace between the United States and Iran, as four regional powers intensify diplomacy ahead of a ceasefire deadline set to expire on April 22.

Abdelatty said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating on a broader regional initiative aimed at preventing further escalation and building a post-conflict security arrangement. He stressed the need to protect Gulf nations and ensure the stability of energy markets, supply chains, and food security.

item.title: US says 21 ships turned back under Iran blockade
item.description: The United States Navy has compelled 21 vessels to reverse course since the start of a naval blockade on Iranian ports, US Central Command announced on Friday, as enforcement operations expanded into open waters and began disrupting Iranian oil shipments well beyond the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran says no new talks until framework agreed
item.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh on Saturday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims about enriched uranium, declaring that Tehran will not hand over its stockpiles to the United States and that no date has been set for a new round of negotiations. Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomatic Forum in Turkey, Khatibzadeh said the Iranians were not ready for face-to-face talks because the American negotiating position had not changed.

"Until we agree on the framework, we cannot set the date," Khatibzadeh told reporters, according to Reuters. His remarks came days after Trump said on April 16 that the United States was "very close" to a deal and that Iran had "agreed to almost everything," including handing over its enriched uranium stockpile.

item.title: NATO chief Rutte calls US withdrawal speculation 'absurd'
item.description:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has pushed back against growing speculation that the United States could leave the alliance, declaring in an interview published by German newspaper Welt am Sonntag that he does not foresee such a departure. "I don't see the USA leaving NATO," Rutte said, calling the speculation "absurd."

The remarks come after weeks of heightened anxiety across European capitals following President Donald Trump's repeated threats to reconsider US membership in the nearly eight-decade-old defense bloc. Trump told Reuters in early April that he was "absolutely" considering trying to withdraw the US from NATO, criticizing allied nations for what he described as insufficient support during the war against Iran.

item.title: U.S. prepares to board Iran-linked ships worldwide
item.description:
The U.S. military is preparing to board Iran-linked oil tankers and seize commercial vessels in international waters within the coming days, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, marking a sharp expansion of the naval pressure campaign against Tehran beyond the Middle East.

The move comes as the Trump administration's Operation Economic Fury enters a new phase, extending enforcement of the naval blockade of Iranian ports — now in its sixth day — to a global maritime pursuit of vessels tied to Iran's oil trade. A temporary ceasefire between Washington and Tehran is set to expire next week.

item.title: Iran fires on Indian-flag ships after reclosing Hormuz strait
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reversed the country's decision to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, reimposing restrictions on the critical waterway and firing on two Indian-flagged vessels attempting to pass through — a sharp escalation that deepened uncertainty over global energy supplies as the 49th day of the U.S.-Iran war drew to a close.

item.title: Trump Organization plans 70-story tower in Tbilisi, Georgia
item.description:
The Trump Organization is planning to build a roughly 70-story luxury residential tower in Tbilisi, Georgia, a project that would become the tallest building in the country's capital and mark the family business's latest international venture during Donald Trump's second term in office.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the project on Friday, with Reuters confirming that "Trump Tower Tbilisi" will be a mixed-use development branded by the Trump Organization in partnership with local developers. Details about the specific Georgian partners involved, the project's estimated cost, and its expected timeline have not yet been fully disclosed.

item.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, deepening jet fuel crisis
item.description: The war in Iran has pushed the global aviation industry to a breaking point, with jet fuel prices nearly doubling since the conflict began and airlines across Europe, Asia, and North America now canceling flights and grounding aircraft as supplies dwindle.

item.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea
item.description:
North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile eastward on Sunday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed, in the latest in a rapid succession of weapons tests that have heightened tensions across the Korean Peninsula this year.

The JCS said it detected the missile launch and was analyzing details of the firing, including its range and flight characteristics. The AFP, citing Yonhap, reported that the South Korean military had tracked the missile heading toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.

item.title: Iran calls free transit through Hormuz 'a fiction' as Europe plans naval mission
item.description: Iran pushed back forcefully against European calls to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, even as dozens of countries gathered in Paris a day earlier to plan a multinational naval mission to restore free passage through one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.
